parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReserveSpotService is an application-layer use case, and most of what it does is the coordination expected there: it calls SpotRepository, ReservationRepository and PaymentPort and uses domain behaviour (Reservation.clashesWith, spot.priceFor). But its public use-case method, reserve(...), takes `request?: Request`, which is Express's HTTP request type. Handling HTTP requests belongs to the presentation (inbound adapter) layer. Putting it in the use-case signature ties the application contract to one web framework, even though the parameter is never used. The import itself is out of scope; the violation is that the method's responsibility includes an HTTP request. A smaller point: the 1–24 hour duration rule is a fixed business rule about reservations and arguably belongs in the domain Reservation entity, not the service.
